peer_results.rationale: AMD's candidate disclosures concern future minimum lease payments and a general definition of purchase commitments (noncancellable purchase orders). Neither addresses minimum purchase obligations for factory output or volume-related damages associated with a specific semiconductor manufacturing co-investment program like Intel's Ireland SCIP disclosure.

AVGO's candidate disclosure defines purchase commitments as unconditional, legally binding obligations for goods or services (primarily inventory) but excludes cancelable agreements and short-term obligations. It does not disclose specific minimum quantity purchase obligations for semiconductor factory output or co-investment program damages comparable to Intel's Ireland SCIP note.

comparisons.peer_summary: As of August 29, 2024, the company had approximately $6.7 billion in noncancelable purchase obligations with remaining terms exceeding one year, primarily covering fixed or minimum quantity/price payments for goods, services, and property, plant, and equipment, with payments scheduled annually from 2025 through 2030 and thereafter.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron disclose obligations to purchase minimum quantities of goods or services with remaining terms exceeding one year, though the specific nature and structure differ. Intel's obligation is tied to a specific semiconductor co-investment program (Ireland SCIP) for Fab 34 output, triggering volume-related damages if minimums are not met, with obligations starting upon construction completion or Q3 2027. In contrast, Micron discloses a broader portfolio of noncancelable purchase obligations totaling approximately $6.7 billion, which include payments for goods, services, and property, plant, and equipment with fixed or minimum quantities and prices, scheduled over a multi-year horizon (2025-2030+).

sentences.text: We will be required to purchase minimum quantities of the related factory output from Ireland SCIP, or we will be subject to pay certain volume-related damages to Ireland SCIP, beginning at the earlier of when construction is complete or Q3 2027.

As of August 29, 2024, we had noncancelable commitments with remaining contractual terms in excess of one year of approximately $6.7 billion for purchase obligations, of which approximately $1.7 billion will be due in 2025, $1.7 billion due in 2026, $1.0 billion due in 2027, $800 million due in 2028, $200 million due in 2029, and $1.3 billion due in 2030 and thereafter.
Purchase obligations primarily include payments for goods or services with either a fixed or minimum quantity and price, which includes payments for the acquisition of property, plant, and equipment.
